REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JULY 12, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON JULY 12, 2018,
IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Soccer Team Hurricanes.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Steve Koffroth expressed concerns regarding a deduction of CalPERS benefits
  from City staff and the halt of deductions of employee Union dues, resulting from
  the recent Supreme Court ruling of the Janus vs. AFSCME case. He requested
  that the City reimburse the union for deductions not taken.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Direct City management staff to conduct an
  informal meeting with the executive leadership of Local 619 AFSCME bargaining
  unit and report back to the City Council.

  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt AN INTERIM ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS EXTENDING THE MORATORIUM ON NEW OR EXPANDED
  SELF-STORAGE FACILITIES AND THE ISSUANCE OF BUILDING PERMITS, USE
  PERMITS, AND OTHER LAND USE ENTITLEMENTS RELATED THERETO WITHIN THE
  CITY FOR AN ADDITIONAL TEN (10) MONTHS AND FIFTEEN (15) DAYS (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  John Bowen expressed concerns regarding the public demand for storage and stated he
  would donate 10 acre-feet of water rights if his project is permitted to be exempt from the
  moratorium.

  Gene Sais requested the City Council exempt his pending storage facility from the
  moratorium.

  Jenny Rocci, Johnson Development, expressed a desire to partner with the City and
  requested an exemption from the moratorium.

  Mary Buell spoke in support of the new storage facility, if the design and hours of
  operation could be altered.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public
  hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Approve and issue a ten (10) day report on the forty-five (45) day
  moratorium on new and expanded self-storage facilities, established by
  way of City Council Ordinance No. 1020; and

  2.  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1021, AN INTERIM
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS EXTENDING THE
  MORATORIUM ON NEW OR EXPANDED SELF-STORAGE
  FACILITIES AND THE ISSUANCE OF BUILDING PERMITS, USE
  PERMITS, AND OTHER LAND USE ENTITLEMENTS RELATED
  THERETO WITHIN THE CITY FOR AN ADDITIONAL TEN (10)
  MONTHS AND FIFTEEN (15) DAYS (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  July 12, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 9

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of a request for consent to the assignment of a ground
  lease and approval of an estoppel certificate and lender consent in connection with
  the assignment of the ground lease interests of a property located at 12800 Center
  Court Drive, Cerritos, California, 90703 from SCE Cerritos LLC, a Delaware Limited
  Liability Company, to the following entities acting collectively as the buyer: Pacific
  Service Company Inc., a Washington Corporation; PVP Investments, LLC, a Delaware
  Limited Liability Company; WCCP Baseline Crossings LLC, an Arizona Limited Liability
  Company; WCCP Arrowhead Park Place LLC, an Arizona Limited Liability Company;
  and, WCCP Cerritos LLC, an Arizona Limited Liability Company, or another affiliated
  entity which has been approved by the City (APN# 7030-011-915) (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager and Dennis
  Roy, Legal Counsel. A PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Thomas Irish, President of Transpacific Development Company, thanked the City for a
  longstanding partnership and expressed his appreciation toward City Council and
  staff.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize the City
  Manager, or his designee, to execute the document(s) to facilitate, acknowledge and
  consent to the transfer of the ground leases of the Cerritos Towne Center office
  building located at 12800 Center Court Drive, Cerritos, CA 90703, from SCE Cerritos
  LLC to Pacific Service Company Inc., PVP Investments, LLC, WCCP Baseline Crossings
  LLC, WCCP Arrowhead Park Place LLC, and WCCP Cerritos LLC, or another affiliated
  entity which has been approved by the City, in such form as the City Manager shall
  deem appropriate, including any estoppel certificates, assignment consent, or related
  implementing documentation required or appropriate in connection with completion of
  such assignment in the forms attached hereto or such other form as the City Manager
  shall deem appropriate (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A JOINT RESOLUTION OF

  1.  Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2018-13, A RESOLUTION

  BETWEEN THE BOARD OF ADMINISTRATION CALIFORNIA PUBLIC
  EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM AND THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS (COUNCIL); and

  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AUTHORIZING AN
  AMENDMENT TO THE CONTRACT BETWEEN THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE BOARD OF ADMINISTRATION OF

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  Edwards, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  July 12, 2018

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  Review and consideration of CalMet Services’ request for an adjustment to the
  Solid Waste Management Program maximum rate limits (COUNCIL).

  A report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager.  A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Bill Kalpakoff, CalMet representative, expressed appreciation for  the
  partnership with City staff.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum expressed concern regarding the consequences of not
  approving a rate limit increase.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor
  closed public comments.

  MOTION TO DENY: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to
  deny CalMet Services’ request to adjust the maximum rate schedule for solid
  wasted services in the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL):

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  Edwards, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of authorization of expenditures for the emergency
  repair of the methane gas extraction system at Bettencourt Park (COUNCIL).

  A report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager.  A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Make a finding that emergency repairs to the Bettencourt Park Methane Gas
  Extraction System are necessary to maintain the safety of the park and the
  adjacent neighborhood; and

  2.  Authorize the expenditures of approximately $40,000 for the necessary
  repairs to the Bettencourt Park Methane Gas Extraction System; and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute changes in the scope
  of work and related expenses if necessary (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to authorize the City

  A report was given by Ramzi Raufdeen, Electric Utility Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  (continued on next page)

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Direct staff to use 4000K, 100W equivalent LED street lights for residential

  2.  Direct staff to use 4000K, 100W equivalent LED street lights for arterial

  3.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to submit LED street light color and

  QUALITY ACT (CEQA) AND DIRECTING THE FILING OF A NOTICE OF
